name: AC (DOXOrubicin / Cyclophosphamide)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: The anthracycline/alkylator AC cytotoxic backbone is not biomarker-restricted; it is used across HR-positive/HER2-negative and HR-negative/HER2-negative (TNBC) early breast cancer, and the same doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide backbone underlies HER2-positive anthracycline-containing regimens combined with HER2-targeted therapy (a separate protocol). ER, PR, and HER2 are tested to guide the addition of endocrine therapy (HR-positive) and HER2-directed therapy (HER2-positive), not to select the AC backbone itself. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer, Preoperative/Adjuvant Therapy Regimens (BINV-M 2 and 3 of 10) and Systemic Therapy (BINV-N).

histology: invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC))

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: give before chemotherapy. DOXOrubicin plus cyclophosphamide (AC) is an anthracycline/alkylator combination; select antiemetic prophylaxis per the NCCN emetic-risk framework (Appendix D categories: high >90%, moderate >30 to 90%). The exact per-regimen emetic-risk tier is designated in the NCCN Antiemesis guideline / order template (not established in the provided sources).

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide combination; provide prophylaxis per NCCN emetic-risk framework (Appendix D). Specific tier per NCCN Antiemesis order template.

G-CSF: AC every 21 days is not flagged for mandatory myeloid growth factor support in the NCCN dosing table (no footnote n); assess febrile-neutropenia risk per NCCN Myeloid Growth Factors framework (Appendix C: High vs Intermediate risk), physician-patient discussion.
monitoring: LVEF at baseline and cardiac monitoring during anthracycline therapy (BINV-M 1 of 10)
liver and renal function before each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: cumulative DOXOrubicin approaching 450 mg/m2 (warn) or 550 mg/m2 (hard cap)
doseModificationRules.text: Track cumulative lifetime anthracycline exposure; approaching 450 mg/m2 warrants review and 550 mg/m2 is the conventional hard cap due to cumulative cardiotoxicity (DeVita 12th ed. lines 19908 to 19919). Physician decides.
Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 6 of 10. DOXOrubicin 60 mg/m2 IV day 1, cycled every 21 days for 4 cycles. ISMP tall-man. Anthracycline cumulative lifetime cardiotoxicity cap applied (warn 450 / hard 550 mg/m2); DeVita 12th ed. describes cumulative-dose-dependent anthracycline cardiomyopathy (lines 19908 to 19919), including cardiomyopathy at total doxorubicin above 340 to 380 mg/m2 when paclitaxel precedes doxorubicin (line 19913 to 19914).

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 6 of 10. Cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 IV day 1, cycled every 21 days for 4 cycles.
